transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place for this. 

I guess I came in because I just... I can't seem to stop worrying about everything at once. I know everyone gets stressed, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, but my mind just keeps racing. I'm constantly worrying about my marriage, and, well, whether I'm slipping at work. I'm in tech, and things move fast, you know? And then I start stressing over the bills, and these house projects I keep starting and then just dropping. 

It's embarrassing to admit, but I just keep having this thought that I'm basically failing as a husband and a father. I'm sorry, I know that's a lot to dump on you right away. Does that make sense, though? Am I explaining it okay?
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these worries been constant for a long time, or did they start more recently in response to specific stressors?

Um, well... I'd say it's been going on for about nine months now. I hope that's the kind of timeline you're looking for. 

It really seemed to start when this huge cloud migration project ramped up at work. You know how those things go, it's a lot of moving parts and long hours, so I figured I was just reacting normally to the workload. Everyone on the team was feeling the crunch, so I really didn't want to make a big deal out of it or be the one complaining. 

But, um... around that same time, my wife and I started having some... well, some disagreements. I hate even bringing it up because I don't want to make it sound like we have a bad marriage or anything. She's incredibly patient with me. It's just that the arguments started becoming a regular thing at home right around then, too, and I just haven't been able to shake this feeling since. 

I probably should have just pushed through it and handled it better on my own by now. Is it normal to let things get to you for that long?
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, fatigue, trouble concentrating, muscle tension, or sleep problems along with these worries?

Um, yeah, I suppose I have noticed a few physical things. I mean, I sit at a computer for a living, so I'm sure it's pretty normal to get a little stiff, but... I just feel wound so tight almost all day. It's like my shoulders are completely locked up, almost like I'm constantly bracing for something. I feel kind of bad even complaining about it, since I know everyone gets stressed. 

And, um, as for the restlessness... I try to keep it under control so I don't annoy my coworkers or my wife, but I keep catching myself pacing back and forth between meetings. Even when I'm trying to unwind at my chess club, I'm just constantly tapping the pieces. Sitting still just feels basically impossible right now. 

I hope it's okay that I mentioned the chess club thing. Does that sound like the kind of muscle tension and restlessness you were asking about?
Do you find that your worrying feels uncontrollable or that you can't seem to stop, even when you want to?

Um, yeah... I really try to just shut it off, I promise. I don't want to be like this. But it... it does feel pretty out of my hands. 

Like, even when I tell myself to just focus on the code right in front of me, or, you know, just breathe through a workout and clear my head, it doesn't really work. It's like... one concern just hooks onto another one. And before I even realize it, I'm twenty steps ahead. I'll start by worrying about a bug in my code, and then suddenly I'm imagining getting a bad performance review, and then getting fired, and then... well, my family just being completely ruined because I couldn't keep it together. 

I know it sounds so irrational when I say it out loud. I really try to just be positive and logical about it, but it just spirals so fast. Is it... is it normal to not be able to just snap out of it like that?
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about multiple areas of your life, not just specific things, like work or family, but many different parts of your life at the same time?

Um, well, yes... I guess that's really the main reason I'm here. I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining about everything, because I know I have a good life, but... it really does feel like it's everything all at once. 

Like, I'll be worrying about work and whether I'm slipping on this migration project, but at the exact same time, I'm stressing over my marriage and the arguments we've been having. And then I start thinking about the bills, and those half-finished house projects I keep dropping because I'm so exhausted... and then it all just kind of snowballs into this awful feeling that I'm basically failing as a husband and a father. 

I really try to keep it all in perspective, I promise. I know it's probably too much to put on you, but... is it helpful to know that it's all those things at the same time? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in activities you usually enjoy, like your chess club or time with your family?

Um, no, I don't think I've really felt hopeless or anything like that. I mean, I still go to chess club, and I definitely still love my family. I wouldn't say I've lost interest in them at all. 

I know I've been talking a lot about how stressed I am, and I hope I didn't make it sound like I'm depressed or giving up. I really do try to stay positive and keep up with everything. It's just... I guess it's just the worrying that gets in the way sometimes, making it hard to fully relax when I am doing those things. But I still want to do them, I promise. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, because I definitely don't feel like I'm hopeless.

latest_inference.note: The patient denies symptoms of depression such as feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in previously enjoyed activities, which rules out F32.0 (Major Depressive Disorder, single episode), F43.00 (Acute Stress Reaction), and F43.20 (Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety). Symptoms are consistent with F41.1 (Generalized Anxiety Disorder) with excessive worry across multiple domains, physical symptoms of anxiety, and difficulty controlling the worry.
